body.p: REMARKS

This Amendment is responsive to the Office Action dated March 21, 2023. Applicant has amended claims 1, 7, 18, 23, and 26-30, and canceled claims 6, 9, 22, and 25. Claims 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10-18, 20, 21, 23, 24, and 26-32 are pending upon entry of this Amendment.
The Office Action rejected the previously pending claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as follows:
" Claims 1, 3-6, 18, and 20-32 were rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S.
Publication No. 2005/0115561 Al by Stahmann et al. (hereinafter, "Stahmann") in view
of U.S. Publication No. 2010/0121399 Al by McCabe et al. (hereinafter, "McCabe"), further in view of U.S. Publication No. 2011/009760 Al by Zhang et al. (hereinafter,
"Zhang"); and
" Claim 17 was rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Stahmann in view of MCabe,
further in view of Zhang, further in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No.
2012/0283705 Al by Lee et al. (hereinafter, "Lee").
Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections to the extent the rejections may be

considered applicable to the claims as amended. The applied references, alone or in any proper combination, fail to disclose or suggest the features defined by Applicant's amended claims, and there would have been no apparent reason that would have caused one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the applied references to arrive at the claimed features.
For example, the applied references fail to disclose or suggest "processing circuitry

configured to: periodically determine a respective value for each of a plurality of physiological parameters based on one or more of [] heart sounds or [an] ECG, wherein at least a first physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the heart sounds and at least a second physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the ECG, wherein the first physiological parameter comprises a frequency of occurrence of an S3 heart sound; ... and determine whether to present an indication of a heart failure event based on an analysis of the trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters," as recited by amended independent claim 1, or the similar recitations of the other amended independent claims.

In rejecting previously pending claims that recited an S3 heart sound (e.g., claims 6, 7, 9, 22, 23, 25, 28, and 30), the Office Action cited paragraphs [1273], [1502], and [1520] of Stahmann. The paragraphs of Stahmann cited in the Office Action do not even relate to heart sounds, much less an S3 heart sound. Paragraph [1265] of Stahmann mentions S3 heart sounds in a listing of "[a] representative set of symptoms and/or physiological changes associated with non-rhythm pulmonary diseases ... ." Paragraph [1494] of Stahmann discloses S3 in a list of "[e]xamples of data acquired during non-sleep that may aid in nocturnal therapy and diagnosis. . ." Paragraph [1512] of Stahmann discusses the S3 heart sound, and states "[a]fter age 40, it almost always indicates the failing heart in congestive heart failure."

However, none of this description from Stahmann discloses or suggests "processing circuitry configured to: periodically determine a respective value for each of a plurality of physiological parameters based on one or more of the heart sounds or the ECG, wherein at least a first physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the heart sounds and at least a second physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the ECG, wherein the first physiological parameter comprises a frequency of occurrence of an S3 heart sound; ... and determine whether to present an indication of a heart failure event based on an analysis of the trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters," as recited by amended independent claim 1, or the similar recitations of the other amended independent claims. Nor do the other cited references disclose or suggest these features of the amended independent claims. For at least this reason, independent claims 1, 18, 27, and 29 are patentable over the cited references. The dependent claims incorporate the requirements of the respective independent claims.1 Accordingly, the dependent claims are likewise patentable.

For at least these reasons, the Office has failed to establish aprimafacie case for non- patentability of Applicant's claims 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10-18, 20, 21, 23, 24, and 26-32 under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Applicant therefore respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.
CONCLUSION
All claims in this application are in condition for allowance. Applicant does not

acquiesce as to any assertion in the Office Action with respect to the cited art or to Applicant's claims. Applicant's silence with respect to any assertion in the Office Action should not be interpreted as Applicant's acquiescence thereto. Applicant reserves the right to comment further with respect to the applied references and any pending claim in a future Amendment, Response, or on appeal. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and prompt allowance of all pending claims.

Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Amendment are unpatentable over the art cited by the Office Action. While several distinctions have been noted over the art of record, Applicant notes that there may be several other limitations that are neither taught nor suggested by the art of record. Applicant expressly reserves all rights and arguments with respect to distinctions not explicitly noted herein. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office in the pending Office Action has not been explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper.
